svg.title: Where Praxis writes, depending on whose repository it is
svg.desc: Six artifacts, compared row by row across the two workspace modes. Operating brief: owner writes CLAUDE.md plus nested files, contributor writes CLAUDE.local.md and leaves the project's own CLAUDE.md untouched. Settings: .claude/settings.json, versus .claude/settings.local.json. Praxis config: a committed .praxis.toml, versus .claude/.praxis/praxis.toml. Docs, CHANGELOG, ADRs and design artifacts: created and kept current, versus joined only if the project already has them and otherwise kept in .claude/.praxis/knowledge/. Ignore rules: Praxis's paths are added to .gitignore, versus .gitignore never touched. Delivery: a commit, a pull request and the merge policy, versus a commit and a pull request in the project's own style, then stop. A closing band states that none of it can reach their history: the artifacts are excluded in the per-clone exclude file, so git status cannot see them and git add -A cannot reach them; the guard refuses to stage a Praxis artifact, -f included, in either mode; and a stage-everything command is verified rather than trusted, with the exclusion repaired or the command blocked. The mode is detected offline from a remote, real history, and no commit from your git address, and /praxis:config mode owner overrides it.

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: commit and PR in their style,
NONE OF IT REACHES THEIR HISTORY
excluded per clone: invisible to git status, unreachable by git add -A
the guard refuses to stage a praxis artifact, -f included, in either mode
and a commit is refused while one is in the index, however it got there
Detected offline: a remote, real history, and no commit from your git address.
The session audit states the verdict and its reason every time; /praxis:config mode owner overrides it.
